title: QuantumNous/new-api — A unified AI model hub for aggregation & distribution. It supports cross-converting various LLMs into OpenAI-compatible, Claude-compatible, or Gemini-compatible formats. A centralized gateway for personal and enterprise model management.
content:
An AI gateway for models, applications, and agents
简体中文 | 繁體中文 | English | Français | 日本語
Capabilities • Quick start • Deployment • Development • Documentation
New API is a self-hosted AI gateway for applications, agents, and teams. Connect upstream model services, expose a consistent API to your clients, and manage routing, access, usage, and costs in one place.
Use it to share authorized model access across a team, switch providers without configuring every client again, or operate a private multi-model service with a web console. Upstreams include OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini, Azure OpenAI, AWS Bedrock, Vertex AI, DeepSeek, Qwen, and other compatible services.
Important
- This project is intended solely for lawful and authorized AI API gateway, organization-level authentication, multi-model management, usage analytics, cost accounting, and private deployment scenarios.
- Users must lawfully obtain upstream API keys, accounts, model services, and interface permissions, and must comply with upstream terms of service and applicable laws and regulations.
- Users should ensure their use complies with upstream terms of service and applicable laws and regulations.
- When providing generative AI services to the public, users should comply with applicable regulatory requirements and fulfill all filing, licensing, content safety, real-name verification, log retention, tax, and upstream authorization obligations required by their jurisdiction.
Warning
When operating this project as a public generative AI service or API resale service, users should first complete all required filing, licensing, content safety, real-name verification, log retention, tax, payment, and upstream authorization obligations.
No particular order
Thanks to JetBrains for providing free open-source development license for this project
RelayKit provides request, response, and streaming conversion between the four text protocols. Available features depend on the channel, upstream model, and conversion path; protocol-specific tools and fields may not map exactly. WebSocket support also requires a compatible upstream and channel configuration.
This README describes the current source tree. Check the release notes for the version you deploy.
This starts a single instance with SQLite and binds it to localhost:
mkdir -p data
docker run --name new-api -d --restart unless-stopped \
  -p 127.0.0.1:3000:3000 \
  -e TZ=Asia/Shanghai \
  -v "$(pwd)/data:/data" \
  calciumion/new-api:latest
Open http://localhost:3000 and complete the setup wizard to create the administrator account. The data directory persists the SQLite database across container replacements.
- Add a channel with your upstream API key, available models, and group assignment; run a channel test.
- Configure model pricing and ensure the user has quota or a valid subscription.
- Create an API key in the console with access to the same group and models.
- Set your client's base URL to http://localhost:3000/v1 for OpenAI-compatible clients and use the New API-issued key.
Set NEW_API_KEY in your shell to that key. List the models accessible to it:
curl --fail-with-body http://localhost:3000/v1/models \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${NEW_API_KEY}"
Then call Responses, replacing your-enabled-model with an enabled model that supports this interface:
curl --fail-with-body http://localhost:3000/v1/responses \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${NEW_API_KEY}" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"your-enabled-model","input":"Hello!"}'
The repository's Compose configuration starts New API + PostgreSQL + Redis by default. It also contains examples for MySQL and a separate ClickHouse log database.
git clone https://github.com/QuantumNous/new-api.git
cd new-api
Before starting, edit docker-compose.yml: replace the database and Redis example passwords in both the services and connection strings, and set a persistent random SESSION_SECRET (generate one with openssl rand -hex 32). For an HTTPS console, configure SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE=true and SESSION_COOKIE_TRUSTED_URL with its exact public HTTPS origin.
docker compose up -d
docker compose logs -f new-api
See the environment example, environment reference, and authentication and session guide for full configuration. Configure container variables in Compose's environment or env_file; copying .env.example alone does not inject variables into the container.
For production, put the console behind HTTPS and configure your reverse proxy for streaming and WebSocket upgrades. Persist and back up the database and mounted data. Multi-node deployments must share the main database and authentication secrets; separate Redis instances or in-memory rate limiters count limits independently per node. The session guide describes propagation behavior for each topology.
Pin an image version from Releases, review its upgrade notes, and back up before upgrading. The latest tag follows published builds and can change; migrations and compatibility must be assessed for your existing installation.
The backend uses Go and Gin. The web console uses React 19, TypeScript, Rsbuild, TanStack, and Tailwind CSS 4. Use Bun for frontend dependencies and scripts; see go.mod for the Go language baseline and Dockerfile for the container build toolchain.
Build the frontend before starting the backend, which embeds web/dist:
# Repository root
cd web
bun install --frozen-lockfile
bun run build
cd ..
go run .
In a second terminal, start the frontend development server:
cd web
bun run dev -- --port 5173
Open http://localhost:5173; the development server proxies API requests to the backend on port 3000. For a containerized development backend, see docker-compose.dev.yml and the make dev target in makefile.
Read AGENTS.md before contributing. Run checks appropriate to your change, including make test for the Go modules and bun run typecheck, bun run lint, bun run test, and bun run build in web/ for frontend changes. Changes to RelayKit must also pass GOWORK=off go build ./... from relaykit/.
For bug reports, include the version, deployment method, reproduction steps, and redacted logs. Documentation, translations, provider integrations, and focused regression tests are all welcome contributions.

report.summary: New API from QuantumNous is a self-hosted AI gateway that unifies OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini and other LLM providers behind one consistent, manageable API.
report.background: Model access has fragmented quickly. Teams now juggle OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Azure OpenAI, AWS Bedrock, Vertex AI and a growing list of Chinese and open-weight providers, each with its own SDK, authentication scheme and request format. Maintaining a separate client integration for every vendor is expensive, and organizations also need centralized keys, quotas, audit trails and cost visibility. New API is a derivative of the widely used One API project (MIT), which popularized self-hosted LLM proxying. QuantumNous extends it with broader protocol conversion, a modern React 19 console and a heavier production stack (PostgreSQL, Redis, optional ClickHouse logs). The project also reflects tightening expectations around lawful gateway operation: teams exposing generative AI publicly must handle filing, licensing, content safety, real-name verification and log retention in many jurisdictions, which makes the gateway a governance layer as much as a routing layer.
key_points: Protocol conversion via RelayKit: the gateway translates requests, responses and streaming between OpenAI-, Claude- and Gemini-style text protocols, so a client written for one vendor can talk to a model from another. The README cautions that conversion is not perfect — provider-specific tools and fields may not map exactly, and WebSocket support depends on the upstream channel.

Broad upstream coverage: supported sources include OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini, Azure OpenAI, AWS Bedrock, Vertex AI, DeepSeek, Qwen and other OpenAI-compatible services. Channels bundle an API key, an allowed model list and a group assignment, which makes swapping providers a configuration change rather than a code change.

Centralized management for teams: a web console handles API-key issuance, user groups, quotas, subscriptions, model pricing, usage analytics and cost accounting. Administrators can share authorized model access across an organization while keeping per-user limits, and clients only ever need one base URL — typically /v1 for OpenAI-compatible tooling.

Flexible deployment: a single Docker command with SQLite runs on localhost for evaluation, while the bundled Compose file starts New API with PostgreSQL and Redis and offers MySQL and a separate ClickHouse log database as alternatives. Production guidance covers HTTPS behind a reverse proxy, WebSocket upgrades for streaming, backups, pinned image versions and shared secrets across multi-node setups.

Licensing and obligations: the project is AGPLv3 with additional Section 7 terms, requiring modified versions to preserve author attribution and a visible link to the original repository. It is built on One API (MIT). Organizations unwilling to accept AGPLv3 obligations are invited to contact the maintainers for an alternative arrangement.
report.impact: Gateways like New API are becoming the control plane of enterprise AI. For the industry, they commoditize individual providers: if any model can be swapped behind one endpoint, competition shifts from SDK lock-in to price, latency and quality. For developers, the practical win is a single base URL and key, meaning tools built for the OpenAI API work with Claude, Gemini or Qwen with minimal changes, and streaming, retries and quota handling are centralized. For regular users inside organizations, it means governed access — budgets, per-team quotas, audit logs and cost reporting rather than scattered personal keys. The trade-offs are real: conversion is lossy for vendor-specific features, the gateway is a single point of failure and a sensitive credential store, and AGPLv3 plus regional compliance duties (filing, content safety, real-name verification) constrain commercial resale.
report.tools: Try New API itself via the single-container Docker quick start, then move to the bundled Compose stack with PostgreSQL and Redis. Useful companions: One API, its MIT-licensed upstream; LiteLLM and Portkey as alternative gateway/proxy layers; OpenRouter for a hosted multi-model option; Helicone or Langfuse for observability and prompt tracing; ClickHouse for large-scale request logging. Review the project's environment reference and authentication/session guide before production deployment.
